title: SRE standards: SLOs, error budgets, capacity planning, and runbooks
author: Jordan Li
body:
Overview:

This page consolidates Redwood Inference SRE standards for Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and error budgets, capacity planning, reliability initiatives, incident review standards, operational tooling, and canonical runbooks. It is intended for oncall engineers, SRE owners, and service owners who need to define, operate, and iterate on production SLOs and runbooks.

Goals:
- Provide a consistent SLO taxonomy and measurement approach across services.
- Define error budget lifecycle and escalation policy.
- Standardize capacity planning inputs, headroom targets, and sizing guidance for GPU-backed inference services.
- Share canonical runbooks and incident review checklist to improve mean-time-to-detect and mean-time-to-recover.

1) SLO taxonomy and examples

SLO types (recommended):
- Availability (success rate): percentage of successful responses for user-facing endpoints (HTTP 2xx / expected response).
- Latency: % of requests below a latency target (p50/p95/p99 as appropriate).
- Correctness/quality: model-level quality metric evaluated by periodic evals (e.g., synthetic prompt pass-rate).
- Throughput/Capacity: service-level throughput SLO for reserved lanes (e.g., Dedicated pool throughput).

Service SLO example (in practice, each service must publish its own values):
- service_name: inference-api-v1 (public REST endpoint)
  - Availability SLO: 99.95% success rate (30d rolling window) for /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings
  - Error budget: 0.05% of requests per 30d (~36 minutes of downtime equivalent per month)
  - Latency SLO: 95th percentile of request latency < 300ms for small-inference tier (prompt tokens <= 512)
  - Quality guardrail: synthetic prompt-set pass rate >= 98% (weekly evaluation)

SLO measurement rules:
- Use the client-observed success metric where feasible (edge success). If that is not available, use gateway metrics with documented delta to client-observed.
- All SLOs must specify: objective, window (30d rolling unless service has a different agreement), measurement source (metrics name and exporter), and owner.
- Error budget is computed as (1 - SLO) * window volume. Track budget burn in % and minutes.

2) Error budget lifecycle and escalation

Error budget phases:
- Healthy (burn rate <= 1x expected): normal operations.
- Degraded (burn rate 1x-3x): notify stakeholders, pause non-essential launches.
- At-risk (burn rate 3x-10x): require action plan, freeze non-critical releases, increase oncall coverage.
- Exhausted (burn rate > 10x or budget depleted): schedule an immediate incident review, emergency rollback, and dedicated debug sprint.

Escalation policy (example):
1) Alert when 7-day burn rate > 2x or remaining budget < 20% -> Pager to service SRE and PM, #incidents channel post.
2) If burn rate > 5x for 1h or remaining budget < 5% -> Paging escalation: primary SRE, SRE manager, and service owner.
3) If budget exhausted -> Trigger incident response runbook and 4-hour blitz to recover.

Actions tied to budget state (owner: service owner + SRE oncall):
- Pause feature launches and canary rollouts.
- Increase diagnostic sampling (traces, logs) and enable high-cardinality tracing for affected paths.
- Deploy hotfixes or roll back recent changes that correlate with increased error rate.

3) Capacity planning and GPU pool sizing

Principles:
- Plan for steady-state QPS + 2x burst headroom for 95th percentile traffic.
- Maintain at least 20% spare capacity headroom for scheduled maintenance and autoscaler lag.
- Reserve separate Dedicated GPU pools for latency-sensitive vs batch workloads.

Inputs required for planning (per-service):
- Baseline QPS (p50/p95) by time-of-day and region (30d historical).
- Typical request token distribution (latency-sensitive vs long-context).
- Target SLO (latency + availability).
- Autoscaling policies and warm-up times (cold-start time for model shards).
- Instance efficiency (tokens/sec per GPU) and expected degradation at high concurrency.

Sizing example (inference-api-v1):
- Observed p95 QPS (global) = 120 QPS
- Average tokens per request = 200
- Throughput per A100-80GB GPU at configured concurrency = 4000 tokens/sec -> ~20 requests/sec equivalent
- Baseline GPUs required = ceil(120 / 20) = 6 GPUs
- Add 2x burst headroom for 95th percentile -> target fleet = 12 GPUs
- Add 20% spare capacity -> operational target = 15 GPUs

Operational guidance for autoscaling and Reserved capacity (Dedicated):
- Early-warning: scale-up at 75% utilization sustained for 5 minutes.
- Aggressive-scale: scale-up at 85% utilization sustained for 1m with pre-warm if possible.
- Scale-down threshold: <40% sustained for 10m.
- For Dedicated contracts, provision explicit buffer of commit_capacity * 1.2 and use burst credits for > commit.

4) Reliability initiatives and improvement targets

Quarterly reliability OKRs (example):
- Reduce P95 latency by 15% for small-inference tier by end of Q2 (owner: serving-runtime)
- Reduce mean time to restore (MTTR) for production errors from 45m to 30m (owner: eng-sre)
- Decrease high-priority incidents caused by deploys by 50% via deployment safety checks and automated rollbacks (owner: eng-platform)

Common initiatives:
- Prefix/KV cache effectiveness improvements and monitoring (measure cache hit rate per model and prompt prefix).
- Run regular load tests tied to SLOs and capacity plans (monthly for high-traffic services).
- Invest in canary and progressive rollouts with automatic rollback on SLO degradation.

5) Incident review standards and postmortem template

Incident review goals: blameless analysis, timeline clarity, root cause identification, and concrete follow-ups with owners and deadlines.

Required postmortem sections (all must be present within 5 business days):
1) Summary: one-paragraph impact and services affected.
2) Timeline: timeline with timestamps and short bullet actions (UTC).
3) Detection and escalation: who detected, which alerts fired, and paging behaviour.
4) Root cause analysis: clearly state root cause(s) and contributing factors.
5) Corrective actions: list of action items, owners, and due dates.
6) Preventative actions: longer-term projects to avoid recurrence, owners, and success metrics.
7) SLO impact and error budget consumption numbers.
8) External communications: copy of customer-facing status updates if relevant.

Example RCA checklist items:
- Was there a recent deployment within 1h of incident start?
- Did automated rollbacks trigger? If not, why?
- Were alerts tuned with appropriate cardinality to avoid alert storms?
- Did capacity alarms show saturation on host/GPU/IO?
- Are there reproducible testcases to verify the fix?

6) Operational tooling and observability standards

Key signals (must be instrumented and available in dashboards):
- Request rate (QPS), success rate, error count by type, latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99).
- GPU utilization, VRAM pressure, host CPU, disk IO, network egress per node.
- Traces: sample at 1% baseline with increased sampling on errors/slow traces.
- Synthetic checks: multi-region health checks for key paths (generate, embeddings).

Recommended alerting rules (examples in PromQL style):
- Availability: increase in 5m error rate -> sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="inference-api",status!~"2.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="inference-api"}[5m])) > 0.002 && sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="inference-api"}[5m])) > 50
- Latency: p95_latency > 300ms for 10m -> histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="inference-api"}[10m])) by (le)) > 0.3
- GPU saturation: avg(node_gpu_utilization) > 0.85 for 5m -> trigger scaling and owner notification

Operational tools and runbooks must be discoverable via the SRE index page and integrated with the oncall tooling (PagerDuty), chatops (Slack / #oncall), and ticketing (Jira).

7) Canonical runbooks (examples)

Runbook: High error rate on inference-api-v1 (owner: service SRE)
- Symptom: error rate > 0.2% for 5m and > 50 req/min
- Pager: Primary SRE and service owner
- Steps:
  1) Gather metrics: dashboard -> Overview -> inference-api-v1 (QPS, errors, latency, GPU).
  2) Check recent deploys: curl -s https://ci.internal/api/latest-deploy?service=inference-api-v1 | jq .commit
  3) If errors correlate with deploy: rollback via ci command: ci rollback --service inference-api-v1 --to=previous-stable (follow the playbook).
  4) If errors are resource-related: check autoscaler events and node pool status: kubectl get hpa, kubectl get pods -n inference --field-selector=status.phase!=Running
  5) Increase sampling and attach debug traces: set trace-sampling=10% for inference-api-v1 (centralized config).
  6) If degraded for >30m, open Postmortem draft and assign owner.

Runbook: GPU node OOM / VRAM pressure (owner: infra SRE)
- Symptom: OOMKill, model container restarts, or VRAM usage > 95% sustained
- Steps:
  1) Identify impacted nodes: kubectl logs or cloud console -> filter OOM events.
  2) Drain node if necessary: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
  3) Scale up Dedicated pool or burst to on-demand pool per capacity playbook.
  4) Investigate model memory leaks: collect heap/dump and attach to ticket.

8) Runbook hygiene and ownership

- Every service must have an owner for SLOs and runbooks (owner field in service manifest).
- Runbooks must be reviewed quarterly and after any major incident.
- Tests: Each runbook must include a short test procedure that can be executed during game-days (e.g., simulated error, validate detection and paging).

9) Training and game-days

- SREs and service owners must participate in at least two game-days per year covering: canary rollback, high-load autoscaling, and cache corruption scenarios.
- Runbook exercises should be lightweight (1-2h) with a short after-action review and runbook updates recorded.

10) Ownership and contacts

- SLO steward: eng-sre (primary contact: Jordan Li)
- Capacity planning owner: eng-sre + eng-platform (capacity-review board monthly)
- Incident review coordinator: eng-sre manager (Sana Ahmed)

References and related pages:
- See: confluence/eng-sre/sre-slos-error-budgets-and-runbooks.json for the introductory playbook
- See: confluence/eng-sre/sre-slos-capacity-runbooks-2025.json for recent capacity numbers and trends
- Tools: internal dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/sre/slo-overview and https://dashboards.redwood.internal/capacity/inference

Appendix: Example Prometheus alert (yaml snippet)

apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: PrometheusRule
metadata:
  name: inference-api-alerts
spec:
  groups:
  - name: inference.rules
    rules:
    - alert: InferenceHighErrorRate
      expr: (sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="inference-api",status!~"2.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="inference-api"}[5m])) ) > 0.002
      for: 5m
      labels:
        severity: page
      annotations:
        summary: 'High error rate for inference-api ({{ $labels.job }})'

If you have questions or need SLO adjustment for a particular service, open a ticket in the SRE backlog and tag the SLO steward.
